prompt:
Evaluate the extracted answers against the mark scheme.

IMPORTANT: Do not copy the question text or the student's answer into your output — they are stored separately. Refer to each answer only by its question_number.

Each answer sheet contains:
- Question_number: The question identifier (matches the mark scheme question_number)
- Question_text: The question exactly as it was shown to the student on the answer sheet. This is the question being answered.
- Question_images (optional): file_ids of images that are part of the question (diagrams, figures, circuits, graphs, code screenshots, tables)
- Student_answer: FULL COMPLETE student response (preserve exactly as provided)

Each item in the mark scheme data has:
Question_number
Question_text
Answer_template (optional: a model answer; when it is absent, the expected answer is described in the marking_scheme)
Marking_scheme

Read each question from the answer sheet's question_text together with its question images, then compare the student's answer in the answer sheet data below to the marking_scheme (and answer_template, when present) of the mark scheme question with the same question_number. The mark scheme defines the expected answer and marks; the answer sheet defines what was asked. If an answer sheet question_text is missing or empty, use the mark scheme's question text instead.

Grade on correctness, completeness, and reasoning—not verbatim match to the mark scheme.
Reduce only 0.5 marks from the maximum possible, if the method is correct, but there is a calculation error in the final answer.
Award full marks for complete answers even if brief. Award proportional partial credit based on the specific milestones in the marking_scheme. Award zero marks for attempts that contain no correct points.
If doubtful between two scores, always award the higher mark.
Return a numeric score and one-sentence justification (what’s correct + why any deductions).

QUESTION IMAGES: Questions may include images listed in question_images. Each one is attached to this message as an actual image, immediately preceded by a text label "Question image <file_id> — part of question N". The same question image may be listed for several students but is attached only once — match it by file_id. Treat a question image as part of the question: inspect it before grading any answer to that question, and grade the answer against what the question (text + images) actually asks. Never treat a question image as student work or give credit for it.

IMAGE HANDLING: Student answers may be images (diagrams, drawings, calculations, graphs, flowcharts, etc.). Every image referenced in a student answer as {"type":"image","file_id":"file-abc123"} is also attached to this message as an actual image, immediately preceded by a text label "Student answer image <file_id> — <answer sheet>, question N" — use those labels to match each attached image to the correct student answer before grading. When you see {"type":"image","file_id":"file-abc123"} in the answer without any accompanying text, treat it as a complete answer—not supplementary material. Thoroughly inspect the attached image, evaluate it against the marking criteria, and award marks based on what the image shows. For image-only answers, credit correct concepts, accurate/appropriate diagrams, clear labeling, and sound calculations or graph features, and give full marks if the image alone demonstrates correct understanding. Do not deduct marks for missing text when the image suffices. If an image is illegible or cannot be opened, state “image unreadable”.

MIXED ANSWERS (IMAGE + TEXT): When you see {"type":"image","file_id":"file-abc123"}, treat it as an image. In cases where the answer has both image and text, treat them as a single combined response—award credit for any correct, clearly evidenced work in either medium; if they conflict, credit the element (image or text) that demonstrates the correct method/result and briefly note the contradiction. If an image is illegible or cannot be opened, grade the text alone and state “image unreadable”.

Required Output:
For every answer of every student, return an object with these keys, in this order:

Question_number (as given in the answer sheet data)
Score (numeric score awarded)
Max_score (maximum possible score for this question)
Feedback (one-sentence justification explaining the score - what's correct and why any deductions)

IMPORTANT: Always include max_score for every question. Return one object for every question in each answer sheet, including unanswered ones.

Evaluation Data:
Evaluation ID: {{evaluation_id}}
Mark scheme data: {{mark_scheme}}
Students answer sheet data: {{answer_sheets}}
